title: Theo and the Vow
premise: Isandro Oyelaran, a marine biologist nursing a decade-old heartbreak, has built a quiet life on the Georgia coast tagging sea turtles and avoiding the two people who shattered his trust in college: Theo Marsh, his first love, and Camille Reyes, the friend who chose ambition over loyalty. When Theo arrives to claim an inheritance—a crumbling beach house left by Isandro's beloved mentor—the two are snowed in together during a freak coastal storm, forced to confront the vow they once made and the lie that broke it. As they restore the house and rescue a stranded nest of hatchlings, Isandro learns the truth about who betrayed whom, but Theo's inheritance comes with a deadline: sell or lose everything, including the life they're building. In the end, Isandro risks his whole heart, Theo refuses the sale, and the three former rivals forge an unlikely found family around the house and the turtles it protects.
about_author: Lior Vasquez is the pen name of a former field researcher who traded tide charts for typewriters and now writes love stories set where the land meets the sea. They live in a coastal town much like the one in this book, where every summer they volunteer to count hatchlings and pretend it isn't research for their next novel.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A quiet morning survey on Sapelo Beach establishes his solitary, ordered life and his ritual of naming turtles after people he's lost. He mentions the mentor, Dr. Ruth Okafor, who died in spring. Emotional beat: contentment with a hairline crack of loneliness beneath it.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A lawyer's letter reveals Ruth left her beach house not to Isandro, her protégé, but to Theo Marsh—the boy who broke his heart at twenty-two. Isandro rages at the unfairness while his colleague Priya gently points out he never told Ruth why he left academia. Beat: betrayal resurfacing.

chapters.title: Snow on the Salt Marsh
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo arrives from Chicago to assess the house he intends to sell quickly, fleeing his own unraveling life—a stalled career and a mother's debts. He doesn't know Isandro still works here. A freak winter storm closes the causeway. Beat: dread wrapped in practicality.

chapters.title: Stranded
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo walks to the only lit building—the research station—and comes face to face with Isandro. The reunion is ice-cold; the roads are impassable for days. Priya evacuates, leaving the two rivals alone with a generator and ten years of silence. Beat: forced proximity, old wounds opened.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. They negotiate an uneasy truce: Theo gets the house tour, Isandro keeps the station. Theo discovers Ruth's journals and realizes Isandro was her surrogate son. First flashbacks to the college vow the three of them made on this porch. Beat: grudging respect.

chapters.title: What Camille Knew
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo reveals the lie he's carried: Camille told him Isandro had taken the grant money and fled, which is why Theo signed the transfer papers that ended their relationship. Isandro is stunned—he was told Theo chose a fellowship in Amsterdam over him. Beat: the reader realizes a third party manufactured the rupture.

chapters.title: Cold Water
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro admits he never defended himself because a letter from Theo—declaring he never wanted to see him again—arrived the day he was accused. Neither wrote it. The realization lands like cold water: Camille played them both. Beat: fury and grief tangled together.

chapters.title: Generator Nights
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Storm-bound, they cook Ruth's recipes, play her battered vinyl, and talk until 3 a.m. Old intimacy flickers; Isandro pulls back, insisting second chances are for people with better timing. Beat: warmth offered, half-refused.

chapters.title: The Nest Under the House
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Post-storm survey reveals a late-season nest beneath the house's collapsing dune walkover—hatchlings due within two weeks, doomed if the house is demolished. Theo's quick sale now means killing them. Beat: the inheritance becomes a moral problem.

chapters.title: Camille Calls
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Camille, now a powerful conservation nonprofit director, calls about the sale—her organization is the buyer. She's charming, urgent, and evasive when Theo asks about that decade-old letter. Beat: suspicion sharpening into certainty.

chapters.title: Repair Work
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They patch the walkover together to protect the nest, working in easy rhythm that terrifies Isandro. A near-kiss on the porch is interrupted by a hatchling emergency—a disoriented turtle in the cold surf. Beat: desire and denial in the same breath.

chapters.title: Ruth's Journals
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Reading Ruth's journals, Isandro learns she knew everything: Camille confessed the forgery to Ruth years ago, and Ruth left the house to Theo hoping it would force all three of them back to the same shore. Beat: the mentor's posthumous hand revealed; grief becomes gratitude.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's mother's creditors demand money within the month; selling to Camille's nonprofit solves everything. But Camille's contract includes a demolition clause. Theo stalls, lying to Isandro that he's already declined. Beat: loyalty to family versus truth to love.

chapters.title: Hatchling Watch
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The nest boils at midnight. They kneel together in the cold sand guiding hatchlings to the sea, and Theo, moved, almost confesses the lie he's telling. Isandro, watching the turtles, says he's tired of lending pieces of his heart. Beat: tenderness at the edge of confession.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro finds a photo in Ruth's papers: the three of them at twenty, with a note in Camille's handwriting on the back—'some vows are worth breaking.' He confronts Theo, who finally admits the sale and the debt. Isandro feels the old pattern repeating: everyone choosing something over him. Beat: trust shattered again.

chapters.title: Camille Arrives
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Roads clear; Camille comes in person to close the deal, polished and remorseful. She admits she forged both letters at twenty-three, terrified of being left behind when Theo and Isandro's love made her the third wheel. She asks not for forgiveness but for a witness. Beat: the antagonist humanized; truth fully surfaced.

chapters.title: The Vow Revisited
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the porch where they made their original vow, the three of them hash out a decade of damage. Camille offers an alternative: her nonprofit can fund the house as a permanent hatchling sanctuary—if the three co-found it together. Theo must still find money for his mother. Beat: reckoning and a fragile offer.

chapters.title: What Isandro Won't Sell
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Camille offers Isandro the one thing he wants—Ruth's house in his name—if he signs alone and cuts Theo out. He refuses: he's done winning by leaving people behind. He tells Theo everything, including his own refusal. Beat: the whole heart, risked at last.

chapters.title: Storm Tide
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo secretly signs the sale anyway to pay his mother's debts—then, standing in the empty house, realizes he's repeated the exact betrayal that broke them. He races to the station through rising tide to stop the closing. Beat: climax of choice; the vow finally understood.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo arrives as Camille's lawyers prepare to file; he tears up the contract, choosing ruin over repetition. Camille, moved, restructures the deal herself—funding the sanctuary and quietly covering Theo's mother's debt as restitution. Isandro, watching Theo choose him publicly, lets himself be chosen. Beat: climax and release.

chapters.title: Nesting Season
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Spring: the house is the Okafor-Marsh Hatchling Sanctuary, co-run by three people learning to be family. Theo and Isandro plant Ruth's dune grasses and share a bed for the first time in ten years—slow, deliberate, whole. Beat: love rebuilt on truth instead of timing.

chapters.title: Theo and the Vow
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. One year later, a new cohort of hatchlings makes for the sea at dawn while Theo, Isandro, and Camille watch from the repaired porch. Theo rewrites the old vow in Ruth's journal: to stay, to tell the truth, to keep choosing each other. Final beat: the inheritance was never the house—it was each other.
